A page rendered from a whisker template

Source: R/page.R
spigot_page.Rd

Describes one page of a spigot_app(): a complete HTML document written as a whisker (Mustache) template. spigot_app() renders it when the page is requested and adds jQuery, shiny.js and spigot.js to its <head>, so the template needs no {{ headContent() }} and no script tags for them.

Usage

spigot_page(template, data = list(), partials = list(), cache = FALSE)

Arguments

template

The template: its text, or the path of a file holding it.

data

A named list of values for the template, or a function that returns one. A function is called for every request, with the request (the Rook environment) if it takes an argument.

partials

A named list of partial templates: text or file paths.

cache

If TRUE, the page is rendered on its first request and that result is served from then on. Needs static data.

Value

An object of class spigot_page, for the pages argument of spigot_app().

Templates

The template must be a full document with a </head> tag (in any case), either in the template itself or in a partial. Shiny's scripts go just before it. A string containing <, {{ or a line break is the template text; any other string is the path of a file holding it, read as UTF-8 when spigot_page() is called. A relative path is relative to the working directory then, which is the app's directory when the app is run with shiny::runApp(). partials follow the same rule.

The template sees only data, never R variables. {{name}} inserts a value with HTML escaped and {{{name}}} inserts it as raw HTML; neither is ever evaluated as R. Escaping covers &, <, > and " but not ', so put values in double-quoted attributes (value="{{name}}"). {{> name}} inserts partials$name, and a partial that is not in partials is an error (spigot does not look for whisker's name.mustache files).

Relative URLs

Relative URLs in every page resolve from the app's root: href="about", href="docs/intro" and src="logo.png" (a www/ file) mean the same on every page, and so do Shiny's own script URLs. For a page below the top level (/docs/intro), spigot puts <base href="../"> (one ../ per level) first in its <head> to do this, so such a template needs a <head> tag. A template with its own <base> keeps it.

A <base> would also send href="#section" links to the app root, so spigot.js keeps plain clicks on them on the page. Other URLs relative to the page itself, such as href="?tab=2", resolve from the root too: write the page's path (href="docs/intro?tab=2").

A request for /about/ is redirected to /about, where the relative URLs resolve as intended.

Examples

home <- spigot_page(
  "<html><head><title>{{title}}</title></head>
   <body><h1>{{title}}</h1>{{> footer}}</body></html>",
  data = list(title = "Home"),
  partials = list(footer = "<footer>spigot</footer>")
)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
api <- spigot_api() |> plumber::pr_get("/hello", function() list(msg = "hi"))
shiny::runApp(spigot_app(pages = home, api = api))
} # }
